evidence_summary: Kit Rae documents the Hohner Tri Dirty Booster as USA-made with the manufacturer unknown; enclosure evidence links it to the Rogue Fuzz family and possibly Guild FW-3/Goya Fury Box production, but no factory attribution is promoted without stronger direct evidence.

Contemporary collector research indicates Hohner's mid-1970s guitar-effect line was likely third-party manufactured; the available evidence does not identify a single factory or justify a Schaller/German attribution.

The Dirty Booster is part of Hohner's Sound Modifier-era effect lineup, but current evidence does not identify its physical factory; retain as an OEM candidate rather than assigning it to Hohner Germany.

Historical sources distinguish the Echolette Vertrieb marketing entity from the physical manufacturers: early Echolette equipment was developed and built by Artur Klemt, while Dynacord assumed development/production after acquiring Echolette in 1969. No specific dirt pedal builder is promoted from this brand history alone.

Dynacord acquired Echolette in 1969 and produced Echolette-branded equipment afterward, but the current evidence set does not establish a specific standalone fuzz/overdrive pedal model attributable to Dynacord; keep as census context only.
